module_title: Enzymes, Types of Respiration, and Blood Composition
introduction: At this level, we identify the specific chemicals (enzymes) that digest our food, and we understand why our muscles cramp up when we run too fast.

core_concepts.title: Digestive Glands and Enzymes
core_concepts.description:
1. Stomach: Secretes the enzyme 'Pepsin' which digests **Proteins**. It also secretes Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) to kill germs. 
2. Liver: The **Largest Gland** in the human body. It produces 'Bile Juice', which breaks down large Fat droplets into smaller ones (a process called Emulsification). 
3. Pancreas: Secretes Trypsin (for proteins), Amylase (for carbohydrates), and Lipase (for fats).

core_concepts.title: Aerobic vs. Anaerobic Respiration
core_concepts.description:
1. Aerobic: Occurs in the presence of oxygen. Yields 38 ATP of energy per glucose molecule. 
2. Anaerobic: Occurs in the absence/lack of oxygen. 
Muscle Fatigue: When we run fast, our muscles don't get enough oxygen. They switch to anaerobic respiration, producing **'Lactic Acid'**. The accumulation of this lactic acid is what causes muscle cramps and severe fatigue.

core_concepts.title: Heart Chambers
core_concepts.description:
The human heart has 4 chambers: 
- Upper 2 Atria (Auricles): Receiving chambers. 
- Lower 2 Ventricles: Pumping chambers. (The 'Left Ventricle' is the thickest and strongest chamber because it has to pump blood to the entire body).

core_concepts.title: Components of Blood
core_concepts.description:
1. Plasma: The liquid part of blood (approx. 55%). 
2. RBCs (Red Blood Cells): Contain 'Hemoglobin' which transports oxygen. 
3. WBCs (White Blood Cells): The 'soldiers' of the body that fight infections and provide immunity. 
4. Platelets: Help in the 'clotting of blood' when we get a cut.

important_entities.name: Gallbladder
important_entities.key_fact: Stores Bile, Does NOT produce it
important_entities.significance: Bile juice is manufactured by the 'Liver', but it is temporarily stored and concentrated in the 'Gallbladder'. Examiners frequently trick students into saying the gallbladder produces bile.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Bile juice is incredibly important for digesting fats, but surprisingly, it **does NOT contain any digestive enzymes** at all. It acts purely as an emulsifier (like soap on greasy dishes).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In one half of a human jaw, the teeth sequence is: 2 Incisors, 1 Canine, 2 Premolars, 3 Molars. Total = 32 teeth.

exam_strategy_tips: A famous State PCS / UPSC question: 'Which is the largest gland in the human body?' Answer: Liver.
